findings.issue: Still open from the last review: the large heading 'Related products and services' sits over one link, 'Terms and Conditions', which is neither a product nor a service, so the tinted band promises more than it gives. Mobile shows the same.
findings.reference: The competitor's onward link says where it leads, inline in its closing copy ('Read the full group story, facility details and ethics standards at PT King Trading.').
findings.fix: In Site Factory, give the section a heading that fits its link (for example 'Related policies'), or link the product and service pages the heading names.

findings.issue: Still open from the last review: the line under the CTA heading ('Send your enquiry to our factory to tell us about the swimwear you are looking for.') says the heading 'Send an enquiry to our factory' again almost word for word, so the band tells the reader nothing new. Mobile shows the same.
findings.reference: Each line of the competitor's closing copy adds a new fact or a next step ('Manufacturing in Bali since 1993. Read the full group story…'), and none repeats its heading.
findings.fix: In Site Factory, rewrite the CTA's body line to give a reason or a next step (what to put in the enquiry, how fast the reply comes) instead of repeating the heading.

findings.issue: At 390 px the closing band crops its wide photo to a near-square window on the woman, so 'Send an enquiry to our factory' and the lead sit right over her head and upper body. The dark overlay keeps the text readable, but the subject is hidden, and moving object-position cannot clear her inside such a narrow window.
findings.reference: On desktop the same band puts its copy over the darker left of the photo and leaves the subject clear on the right. The competitor keeps its title off the main subject of its photo.
findings.fix: Give the cta band a separate photo crop for narrow widths (art-direction), with the subject low or to one side, so the heading and lead fall on an empty part of the photo.
